A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ActionMesh and contain readable main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–C. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction comparisons, qualitative animation results, and component and autoregressive ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports an expanded quantitative comparison, a reference-frame ablation, and qualitative comparisons with AnimateAnyMesh.

M1.justification: The temporal 3D diffusion and temporal 3D autoencoder procedures, masking, attention, objectives, and inference applications remain unchanged. Appendix C adds architectural dimensions without documenting a model modification.

E1.justification: Training sources, Objaverse reconstruction evaluation, Consistent4D, DAVIS, and animation tasks are retained. ActionBench names and enlarges the existing Objaverse evaluation sample; the added mesh-animation examples do not introduce a distinct task or domain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds TRELLIS and per-frame TripoSG, and includes quantitative ShapeGen4D results where v1 compared it only qualitatively. TripoSG previously appeared in an ablation. Appendix A additionally compares against AnimateAnyMesh, substantially expanding the direct comparison set.

E3.justification: The main quantitative evaluation expands from 32 to 128 animated scenes, while v2 explicitly identifies Table 2 as using 32 scenes. New Table 7 varies the reference frame between first, middle, and last. The existing frame counts, rendering, alignment, metrics, and training settings otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds reference-frame sensitivity testing in Table 7. Appendix A adds qualitative motion-expressiveness cases against AnimateAnyMesh. Earlier component, temporal-length, context-window, and failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The added results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the benchmark scores: ActionMesh's CD-3D/CD-4D/CD-M changes from 0.050/0.069/0.137 to 0.053/0.081/0.148, alongside revised baseline scores and added comparator rows. The expanded test sample prevents interpreting these as same-setting performance changes. Reported runtime changes from three to two minutes. Table 7 and Figure 8 add reference-frame and mesh-animation findings; Tables 2–6 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, inflated-attention equation, alignment definitions, and Appendix C metric equations remain unchanged. No theorem, proof, or formal assumption is added or revised.

C1.justification: The introduction and conclusion strengthen the numerical speed claim from three to two minutes. The abstract explicitly names ActionBench, while the central claims about the two-stage method, topology consistency, rig-free animation, and state-of-the-art reconstruction remain.

C2.justification: v2 attributes greater motion expressiveness than AnimateAnyMesh to video-model motion priors while acknowledging slower execution. It also explains first-frame reference advantages through reduced ambiguity and motion blur. Existing topology-change and occlusion limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly specifies layer counts, attention heads, widths, and latent dimensionality. Section 4.1 identifies a single H100 for timing and states that ActionBench is released. The specific camel-GLB folder pointer is removed. These are documentation and access-statement changes; external availability was not verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds Animate3D, SMF, and AnimateAnyMesh citations, expands the animation-related discussion, and positions ActionMesh against AnimateAnyMesh's speed and motion expressiveness. The broader research positioning and existing references are retained.

P1.justification: Targeted edits revise the abstract, baseline description, evaluation discussion, and related work, with new mesh-animation and reference-frame paragraphs. The main section sequence, appendix organization, and method exposition remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains comparator rows and grouping rules; Figure 8 and Table 7 are added. Existing supplementary Figures 8–9 become Figures 9–10 and move within the appendix layout. Their image content is unchanged. Tables 5–6 standardize the metric label from M-CD to CD-M.

improvement.justification: The expanded Table 1 strengthens the empirical assessment by adding quantitative ShapeGen4D and image-to-3D comparisons, while the reference-frame ablation and architectural disclosures improve validation and reproducibility. A limited weakness remains: Table 1 claims broadly faster execution despite reporting two minutes for both ActionMesh and TripoSG. Overall, the additions provide a modest net improvement to the existing paper.
